step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Introduction and epidemiological background section describing leishmaniasis species and incidence in Tunisia, lacking individual patient clinical narrative

step5_concept_grounding: Epidemiological background discussion of cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis in Tunisia

evidence_items.source_quote: In Tunisia, two clinical forms of Leishmaniasis are endemic. Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) results in skin lesions at the site of the infective sandfly bite. Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a more serious systemic infection associated with high morbidity and not negligible mortality rates.
The current report is the first case of a Tunisian immunocompetent adult with both cutaneous and visceral manifestations of leishmaniasis.

rationale: This segmented text is the general introduction and epidemiological background describing leishmaniasis endemicity in Tunisia without an individual patient presentation (the patient is detailed in segment PMC6850740_02). Lacks single-patient clinical claim -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 50-year-old female presenting with cryptococcal meningitis, not leishmaniasis

step5_concept_grounding: Contextual mention of government visceral leishmaniasis drug program in Nepal

evidence_items.source_quote: The government of Nepal provides liposomal amphotericin B (single dose of 10 mg/kg) free of cost to patients with visceral leishmaniasis (VL) .
The relevant government authority refused to provide liposomal amphotericin B to our patient stating that the drug is to be dispensed to patients with VL only, as per the government policy.

rationale: A 50-year-old female presented with cryptococcal meningitis. Visceral leishmaniasis is mentioned solely as institutional administrative context because the hospital sought liposomal amphotericin B from Nepal's government VL program. The patient did not have leishmaniasis -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 55-year-old male presenting with Ramsay Hunt syndrome following antimonial treatment for cutaneous leishmaniasis

step5_concept_grounding: Prior cutaneous leishmaniasis treated with pentavalent antimonials preceding Ramsay Hunt syndrome

evidence_items.source_quote: He had completed treatment with a pentavalent antimonial drug for cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) 40 days prior. A history and physical examination detected an active lesion with satellite papule in the patient's right upper limb.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical history and examination of cutaneous lesion

evidence_items.source_quote: Ten days after the end of treatment, the patient's leishmaniasis lesion was healed (Figure 1). However, it presented with microvesicles grouped on anerythematous base, starting in the neck and ascended towards the scalp margin on the right side of the head.

rationale: A 55-year-old male presented with Ramsay Hunt Syndrome (herpes zoster oticus) following completed antimonial treatment for cutaneous leishmaniasis. The CL lesion had already healed, and the primary medical emergency/subject of the report is Ramsay Hunt syndrome. Leishmaniasis is past history / inciting antecedent treatment without concurrent active infection or specific laboratory confirmation reported -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Literature review and discussion section reviewing cohorts of patients with STAT1 GOF mutations and citing external case series

step5_concept_grounding: Literature review discussion of STAT1 GOF mutation cohorts and visceral leishmaniasis cases

evidence_items.source_quote: In a different study, Dotta et al. found STAT1 GOF mutations in nine patients with CMC.

This report describes and discusses the first case of visceral leishmaniasis in a patient with a STAT1 GOF mutation who did not have CMC or any of the other previously described clinical manifestations and progressed to hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and death.

rationale: This segmented text represents a literature review and discussion section discussing published cohort studies (Depner et al., Dotta et al., Toubiana et al.) of STAT1 GOF mutations rather than an individual patient case presentation. Lacks single-patient clinical claim -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 34-year-old male with an atrophic facial scar from childhood cutaneous leishmaniasis receiving autologous fibroblast transplantation

step5_concept_grounding: Historical scar from childhood cutaneous leishmaniasis treated with fibroblast transplantation

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was a 34-year-old man with a skin lesion caused by cutaneous leishmaniasis on his left cheek in his childhood.

rationale: A 34-year-old male presented for aesthetic treatment (autologous fibroblast transplantation) of an atrophic facial scar from childhood cutaneous leishmaniasis. There was no active infection, and the primary procedure was cosmetic scar repair. Historical resolved infection -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: An 81-year-old male physician presenting with basal cell carcinoma within an inactive leishmanization scar from 52 years earlier

step5_concept_grounding: Basal cell carcinoma arising within a 52-year-old inactive leishmanization scar

evidence_items.source_quote: Dr. K., an eighty-one-year-old physician has been leishmanized at the age of 29 in Martsinovsky Institute of Medical Parasitology and Tropical Medicine (Moscow)
The histopathology was that of a BCC.

rationale: An 81-year-old male developed a basal cell carcinoma in an inactive cutaneous scar resulting from intentional leishmanization performed 52 years earlier. There was no active leishmanial infection; the active clinical disease is cutaneous malignancy -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A male toddler presenting with acute Chagas disease myocarditis caused by Trypanosoma cruzi

step5_concept_grounding: Acute Chagas-related myocarditis caused by Trypanosoma cruzi

evidence_items.source_quote: Later on, a histopathological examination revealed amastigote forms in the myocardial sections (Figure 1), confirming death due to Chagas-related myocarditis.

rationale: A 2-year-old child presented with acute febrile illness and died from acute Chagas-related myocarditis confirmed by myocardial histopathology showing Trypanosoma cruzi amastigotes. Leishmaniasis was never tested, diagnosed, or asserted as a candidate diagnosis for this patient -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 32-year-old male laborer presenting with an ulcerated finger nodule suspected of leishmaniasis

step5_concept_grounding: Ulcerated dermal nodule on finger suspected to be leishmaniasis, diagnosed as fibro-osseous pseudotumor

evidence_items.source_quote: The initial clinical suspicion was leishmaniasis, due to which a punch biopsy was done.
Microscopic sections examined revealed biphasic fibro-osseous lesion present in the dermis, composed of stromal and osseous components.

rationale: A 32-year-old male presented with an ulcerated finger nodule. Cutaneous leishmaniasis was clinically suspected and investigated via punch biopsy, but histological examination conclusively ruled out Leishmania and established a definitive diagnosis of fibro-osseous pseudotumor of the digit. Target disease investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 59-year-old female with HTLV-1 coinfection presenting with ulcerated facial and knee lesions

step5_concept_grounding: Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis in HTLV-1 co-infected host

evidence_items.source_quote: Patient was positive for Montenegro intradermal test and diagnosed with mucocutaneous leishmaniasis and was admitted in the University Hospital in September 2012.

rationale: A 59-year-old HTLV-1 co-infected female had ulcerative cutaneous and malar lesions with positive Montenegro intradermal skin test and primary diagnosis of mucocutaneous leishmaniasis (E2 specific evidence). Treated with amphotericin B before fatal bacterial sepsis. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 59-year-old male with cutaneous ulcers, oral mucosal lesions, and co-existing plantar melanoma

step5_concept_grounding: Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis concurrent with melanoma

evidence_items.source_quote: Patient was Montenegro intradermal test positive and was admitted at the University Hospital in December 2018.
After seven days, we accessed the PCR laboratory test and initiated therapy with intravenous liposomal amphotericin B 50 mg at the dose of 200 mg/kg/day for 15 days ( Figure 4).

rationale: A 59-year-old male presented with mucosal ulcers and cutaneous lesions with confirmed positive Montenegro test and positive PCR for Leishmania (E1 confirmatory evidence), concurrent with a diagnosed plantar melanoma. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 47-year-old male traveler presenting with 10 cutaneous lesions on upper and lower extremities

step5_concept_grounding: Cutaneous leishmaniasis with multiple lesions

evidence_items.source_quote: Samples from our two patients were positive for Leishmaniasis by immunohistochemistry and histopathologic evidence of amastigotes in both cases.

rationale: A 47-year-old male presented with 10 ulcerated skin lesions confirmed positive for Leishmania amastigotes by histopathology and immunohistochemistry (E1 confirmatory evidence). Fully resolved after amphotericin B and miltefosine therapy. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 47-year-old male (Patient 1) presenting with fever of unknown origin, hepatosplenomegaly, and diarrhea

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) caused by Leishmania infantum / donovani

evidence_items.source_quote: The blood mNGS test results on the 4th day of admission detected Leishmania infantum and Leishmania donovani (Figure 2).
evidence_items.target_concept: Leishmania infantum and Leishmania donovani DNA

evidence_items.source_quote: One day later, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention performed an rK39 antibody test and the result appeared positive; therefore, the clinical diagnosis of kala-azar was made, and the patient was subjected to sodium stibogluconate (SSG) treatment.

rationale: A 47-year-old male presented with persistent fever, splenomegaly, and pancytopenia. Blood mNGS detected Leishmania infantum/donovani and rK39 antibody testing was positive (E1 confirmatory and E2 specific evidence). Treated with sodium stibogluconate before multi-organ failure. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 15-year-old male student (Patient 2) presenting with high fever, cough, and splenomegaly

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania infantum

evidence_items.source_quote: On the fourth day, the mNGS test results of the patient showed Leishmania infantum (Figure 4).
CDC was contacted for rK39 antibody test, and the antibody was detected to be positive on the seventh day, which is in accordance with the criteria for clinically diagnosed cases (Aronson et al.,).

rationale: A 15-year-old male presented with persistent high fever and splenomegaly. Blood mNGS detected Leishmania infantum and rK39 antibody testing was positive (E1 confirmatory and E2 specific evidence). Fully recovered after sodium stibogluconate treatment with spleen regression. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 52-year-old female presenting with an ulcerative forearm nodule suspected of CL

step5_concept_grounding: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (ruled out) in favor of small lymphocytic lymphoma / leukemia cutis

evidence_items.source_quote: The skin lesion was initially suspected of being cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) because of its endemism in our country. However, the microscopic examination of the Giemsa-stained smears of skin lesion was negative.
The histopathological examination of the biopsy specimen showed a dense, diffuse, and monomorphous infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis, which rejected the diagnosis of CL.
Finally, the lesion was diagnosed as leukemia cutis (involving stage I of SLL/CLL).
evidence_items.target_concept: Alternative diagnosis: leukemia cutis / small lymphocytic lymphoma

rationale: A 52-year-old female had an ulcerative forearm nodule clinically suspected of cutaneous leishmaniasis. Giemsa-stained smears and histopathological examination were negative and rejected CL, establishing an alternative diagnosis of leukemia cutis (SLL/CLL stage I) responsive to rituximab. Leishmaniasis is explicitly ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old female living with HIV presenting with recurrent tegumentary leishmaniasis ulcers

step5_concept_grounding: Tegumentary leishmaniasis in patient with HIV coinfection

evidence_items.source_quote: In October 2020, she presented a single ulcer lesion in the lower limb [ (Fig. 1)], and the TL diagnosis was confirmed by Giemsa-stained slides from skin scraping.
At that time, a biopsy sample was collected for parasite isolation, resulting in the obtaining of the clinical isolate denominated as BG03.

rationale: A 30-year-old female with HIV co-infection presented with limb ulcerations confirmed as tegumentary leishmaniasis by Giemsa-stained skin scraping and skin biopsy parasite isolation (isolate BG03) (E1 confirmatory evidence). Fully healed after liposomal amphotericin B therapy. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 61-year-old female (Patient 2) presenting with lower limb and nasal dorsum ulcerative lesions

step5_concept_grounding: Tegumentary leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania infantum

evidence_items.source_quote: Parasitological diagnosis on Giemsa-stained slides confirmed diagnosis of TL.
At this point, an isolate was obtained from skin biopsy and referred to as BG05.
The full nucleotide sequences of BG03 and BG05 showed at least 99.8% identity with L. (L.) infantum LD strain sequence, as well as 99.8% identity to each other (Fig. 3).

rationale: A 61-year-old female presented with ulcerated limb and nasal lesions confirmed as tegumentary leishmaniasis by Giemsa microscopy, parasite isolation (BG05), and ITS sequencing identifying Leishmania infantum (E1 confirmatory evidence). Lesions fully healed after miltefosine treatment. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 56-year-old male farmer presenting with high fever, abdominal pain, hepatosplenomegaly, and leukopenia

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania donovani

evidence_items.source_quote: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of the patient's blood sample indicated a coverage of 0.06% of the L. donovani whole genome of L. donovani (Figure 2).
Subsequently, a positive result was obtained using an rK39 dipstick (InBios International, Seattle, WA, USA).

rationale: A 56-year-old male presented with persistent high fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and anemia. Blood mNGS confirmed Leishmania donovani genomic DNA and rK39 dipstick was positive (E1 confirmatory and E2 specific evidence). Fully recovered after sodium antimony gluconate treatment. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 65-year-old male presenting with intermittent fever, splenomegaly, and pancytopenia

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania infantum with pulmonary involvement

evidence_items.source_quote: Leishmania amastigotes were detected by BMA (Figure 1A).
The BALF mNGS reported 8431 Leishmania infantum sequence readings (Figure 2A).

rationale: A 65-year-old male had visceral leishmaniasis confirmed by detection of Leishmania amastigotes on bone marrow aspiration and 8431 Leishmania infantum reads on BALF mNGS (E1 confirmatory evidence). Despite sodium stibogluconate therapy, patient died from multiple organ failure. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A young male child (oldest of two siblings, weight 12 kg, height 97 cm) presenting with epistaxis, splenomegaly, and pancytopenia

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania infantum

evidence_items.source_quote: For microscopy identification, direct examination of the spinal cord cytopic fluids after GIEMSA staining revealed amastigote forms of Leishmania (Figure 1).
PCR performed on December 19, 2019, on extracted DNA from bone marrow showed that Leishmania infantum was the responsible species.

rationale: A pediatric male patient presented with massive splenomegaly, severe anemia, and epistaxis. Direct Giemsa microscopy revealed Leishmania amastigotes and nested PCR on bone marrow aspirate confirmed Leishmania infantum (E1 confirmatory evidence). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 37-year-old male with GATA2 deficiency presenting with refractory visceral leishmaniasis and massive splenomegaly

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis in patient with inborn error of immunity (GATA2 deficiency)

evidence_items.source_quote: ELISA immunoassay and rK39 rapid test was positive.
evidence_items.test_name: ELISA immunoassay and rK39 rapid test

evidence_items.source_quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was performed on the bone marrow aspirate, with a positive result for Leishmania.

rationale: A 37-year-old male with underlying GATA2 deficiency presented with fever, splenomegaly, and pancytopenia. Diagnostic evaluation demonstrated positive ELISA and rK39 rapid tests, and PCR on bone marrow aspirate was positive for Leishmania (E1 confirmatory evidence). Responded to combined antileishmanial therapy. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 13-year-old boy with Griscelli syndrome type II presenting with recurrent visceral leishmaniasis

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis in patient with Griscelli syndrome type II

evidence_items.source_quote: Bone marrow aspirate showed amastigotes of Leishmania.
A bone marrow aspirate was performed, showing amastigotes of Leishmania that were also detected in his bone marrow culture.
evidence_items.test_name: Bone marrow aspirate microscopy and culture
evidence_items.target_concept: Amastigotes and culture promastigotes of Leishmania

rationale: A 13-year-old boy with Griscelli syndrome type II had visceral leishmaniasis confirmed by detection of Leishmania amastigotes on repeated bone marrow aspirates and positive bone marrow culture (E1 confirmatory evidence). Treated with liposomal amphotericin B and secondary prophylaxis. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 29-year-old female presenting with an intranasal lesion misdiagnosed as an intranasal polyp

step5_concept_grounding: Mucosal leishmaniasis of the nasal cavity caused by Leishmania major

evidence_items.source_quote: Microscopic examination revealed spindle-shaped Leishmania promastigote-like structures without any amastigotes of the parasite (Figure 1).
Then, using ITS1-PCR, Leishmania major were identified.

rationale: A 29-year-old female with an itchy recurrent intranasal lesion underwent fine needle aspiration; cytology and subsequent ITS1-PCR definitively identified Leishmania major (E1 confirmatory evidence). The patient received systemic glucantime with complete lesion healing. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 5-year-old female with Down syndrome presenting with extensive disseminated/diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis

step5_concept_grounding: Diffuse / disseminated cutaneous leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania (Viannia) braziliensis

evidence_items.source_quote: Amastigote forms were found during direct microscopic examination (smear test); this procedure was carried out at the National Referral Laboratory of Leishmaniasis of the National Institute of Health since the periodic acid-Schiff stain (PAS) and the differentiation group 1A (CD1A) were negative.
Genomic DNA samples extracted from lesion tissue revealed that the disease was caused by Leishmania (Viannia) braziliensis.

rationale: A 5-year-old female with Down syndrome presented with refractory disseminated ulcers. Parasitological smear demonstrated Leishmania amastigotes, Montenegro intradermal test was positive, and PCR-RFLP confirmed Leishmania (Viannia) braziliensis (E1 confirmatory evidence). The patient improved following liposomal amphotericin B. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 74-year-old male farmer presenting with pancytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly, and fatigue

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania infantum

evidence_items.source_quote: The test results indicated that the Leishmania antibody was positive.
The results showed that 4101 sequence readings were detected for the Leishmania genus, and 98 sequence readings were detected for the Leishmania infantum species.

rationale: A 74-year-old male presented with chronic pancytopenia and progressive hepatosplenomegaly. Diagnostic workup showed positive rK39 antibody test and blood mNGS detecting 98 sequence reads of Leishmania infantum (E1 confirmatory and E2 specific evidence). The patient received sodium stibogluconate with spleen regression. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 43-year-old Venezuelan female traveler presenting with an extensive ulcerated wound on the left lower shin

step5_concept_grounding: Complex cutaneous leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania panamensis

evidence_items.source_quote: After the patient was discharged, the final diagnosis from the CDC PCR of the large skin lesion sample was complex cutaneous leishmaniasis from Leishmania panamensis.

rationale: A 43-year-old female traveler presented with a large ulcerated lower shin wound following an insect bite in Panama. Reference testing at the CDC by PCR definitively diagnosed complex cutaneous leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania panamensis (E1 confirmatory evidence). The patient received miltefosine and liposomal amphotericin B according to CDC guidelines. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A male child (4th of seven children) presenting with necrotizing limb ulcer and fatal shock from cutaneous anthrax

step5_concept_grounding: Differential diagnosis mention of cutaneous leishmaniasis in fatal cutaneous anthrax case

evidence_items.source_quote: An initial diagnosis of cellulitis of the left lower limb with necrotic ulcer was made; differentials included pyomyositis of the thigh, osteomyelitis of the left tibia, cutaneous leishmaniasis, and malignancy with metastasis (soft tissue sarcomas).
evidence_items.target_concept: Differential diagnosis list including cutaneous leishmaniasis

evidence_items.source_quote: However, the diagnosis of cutaneous anthrax was entertained on account of the striking skin lesions and the course of patients' problems before demise which suggested toxemia with shock.
evidence_items.target_concept: Definitive entertained diagnosis: cutaneous anthrax toxemia with shock

rationale: A pediatric male patient presented with an acute necrotic lower limb ulcer and died from septic shock within 72 hours of admission following contact with cattle carcasses. The case was diagnosed as cutaneous anthrax. Cutaneous leishmaniasis was merely listed in a differential diagnosis list, never evaluated or confirmed -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 55-year-old female presenting with multiple chronic nodular lesions localized exclusively to the tongue

step5_concept_grounding: Isolated lingual post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL) caused by Leishmania donovani

evidence_items.source_quote: Although rK-39 serology was positive, its limited sensitivity in mucosal PKDL necessitated molecular confirmation.
Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting L donovani DNA was performed and returned positive, establishing the diagnosis of isolated lingual PKDL.

rationale: A 55-year-old female presented with isolated lingual nodular lesions. Diagnosis of lingual PKDL was established by positive rK-39 serology and positive PCR targeting Leishmania donovani DNA (E1 confirmatory evidence). The patient achieved complete resolution with liposomal amphotericin B. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 36-year-old female migrant worker presenting with prolonged fever, pancytopenia, and massive splenomegaly

step5_concept_grounding: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) caused by Leishmania donovani mimicking SLE

evidence_items.source_quote: Definitive diagnosis was made through direct visualization of intracellular Leishmania donovani parasites in smear of bone marrow aspirate (Figures 2A,B), which was further confirmed by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CCDC).
evidence_items.test_name: Bone marrow aspirate smear direct visualization

evidence_items.source_quote: Molecular confirmation was also achieved by positive Leishmania-specific PCR (Figure 3A).

rationale: A 36-year-old female misdiagnosed with SLE presented with high fever, pancytopenia, and massive splenomegaly. Definitive visceral leishmaniasis was established by direct visualization of intracellular Leishmania donovani amastigotes on bone marrow aspirate and positive Leishmania-specific PCR (E1 confirmatory evidence). Fully resolved after liposomal amphotericin B. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 75-year-old Caucasian male presenting with relapsing mucosal leishmaniasis with oral cavity involvement

step5_concept_grounding: Mucosal leishmaniasis (MCL) of the oral cavity

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathologic analysis and PCR analysis resulted positive for Leishmania.
Furthermore, Giemsa staining clearly visualized numerous intracellular Leishmania amastigotes within macrophages (Figure 2c), providing direct evidence of parasitic infection.
evidence_items.test_name: Giemsa staining of genial mucosa biopsy

rationale: A 75-year-old male presented with recurrent oral mucosal leishmaniasis lesions. Repeated biopsy histopathology, PCR, and Giemsa staining definitively confirmed intracellular Leishmania amastigotes within macrophages (E1 confirmatory evidence). Responded to repeated cycles of miltefosine therapy. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 26-year-old pregnant female presenting with an erythematous tumoral lesion on the nose

step5_concept_grounding: Cutaneous leishmaniasis presenting as a tumoral lesion on the nose

evidence_items.source_quote: Many histiocytes contained tiny, uniform, spherical creatures, which a pathologist determined to be Leishmania amastigotes (Figures 2(a), 2(b)).

rationale: A 26-year-old pregnant female presented with a tumoral nasal mass of 2 years duration. Punch biopsy histopathology confirmed intracellular Leishmania amastigotes (E1 confirmatory evidence). Successfully treated with postpartum intramuscular glucantime and surgical excision with no recurrence at 1-year follow-up. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.
